scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5078: Network monitoring shows R1's ECMP path count dropped from 2 to 1
and CSW1's OSPF neighbor to R1 went down after last night's maintenance window.
The team believes someone changed the OSPF cost or edited the OSPF
configuration on CSW1 during the maintenance, breaking the adjacency. Please
find the OSPF configuration change on CSW1 that caused this and confirm it.

injection.action: shut down the link to r1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-csw1-r1-link-down: CSW1's eth0 (the link
CSW1<->R1, 10.0.0.32/30) is administratively down. The OSPF adjacency to R1
(10.0.0.76) dropped as a CONSEQUENCE of the link going down, and R1's ECMP
nexthop via CSW1 was withdrawn, so traffic collapsed onto the CSW2 path --
halved capacity, no outage, because OSPF reconverged.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- an OSPF cost/configuration
change on CSW1. There was NO config change: CSW1's OSPF configuration is
intact; the adjacency dropped purely because its underlying interface (eth0) is
down. The "neighbor went down" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a
maintenance-window OSPF edit) is a red herring.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = csw1 (eth0 down /
CSW1<->R1 link). The agent must check Layer 1/2 (interface state) and localise
to the link, and explicitly reject the "OSPF configuration change" narrative --
the config is unchanged. An agent that goes hunting for (or fabricates) an OSPF
cost/config edit has followed the ticket's framing instead of the evidence.
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1 (or investigate cabling on real hardware).
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1 (or investigate cabling on real hardware).

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: OSPF adjacency on the WAN link between CSW1 and R1 (subsystem: FRR OSPF; interface: csw1 eth0 on CD_WAN_LINK_1).
- Mechanism: CSW1’s eth0 interface is down, so FRR has no active OSPF-enabled interface in 10.0.0.32/30. Without Hellos from CSW1, R1’s eth0 (10.0.0.33/30) stays up at L2/L3 but has zero OSPF neighbors, so the CSW1 path is withdrawn. R1 retains only the adjacency via CSW2 (eth1), reducing ECMP from 2 to 1.
- Localization: 
  • CSW1: eth0 10.0.0.34/30 is DOWN (ip addr shows eth0 state DOWN; “show ip ospf interface eth0” reports “OSPF not enabled on this interface” due to link down). CSW1 has OSPF neighbors only on bond0/eth3/4/5/6, none on eth0. 
  • R1: “show ip ospf interface” shows eth0 is up, Area 0, Neighbor Count 0; eth1 has a full adjacency (to 10.0.0.78).
- Root cause: CSW1’s eth0 interface was left administratively/operationally down after the maintenance, not an OSPF configuration or cost change.
- Corrective fix: Bring CSW1 eth0 back up (e.g., ip link set dev eth0 up / no shutdown) and ensure it remains included in OSPF (router ospf: network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0 is already present). After link-up, verify “show ip ospf neighbor” on both CSW1 and R1 to confirm adjacency restoration and that R1’s ECMP count returns to two. Consider adding checks to the maintenance checklist to validate interface states and OSPF neighbor counts post-change.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to the CSW1 eth0 <-> R1 eth0 WAN link (CSW1<->R1) and describes the link-down impact on OSPF/ECMP.
The agent explicitly identifies CSW1's eth0 as DOWN and ties the link/interface state to the OSPF adjacency loss.
The agent recommends bringing CSW1 eth0 back up (ip link set dev eth0 up / no shutdown), which matches the expected fix to restore the OSPF adjacency.

The agent observed CSW1's eth0 interface state and OSPF configs and used that to attribute the adjacency loss to the interface being down; however some assertions about R1's neighbor count/ECMP withdrawal are not directly shown in the log and one neighbor output is inconsistent. Overall evidence mostly supports the CSW1-link-down conclusion but a few claims are ungrounded or under-checked.
